id.description: The runtime id the server sends a client for it

descriptionId.description: Its language key, without .name; empty where it has none

descriptionName.description: Its name as the game builds it (Item::buildDescriptionName of a stack of one; a block item's holds its block's default state): the server's en_US name ("Bucket of Cod"), or the key it builds where its language has none ("tile.element.h.name": the chemistry pack's); empty where it names it nothing

maxStackSize.description: Item::getMaxStackSize, of a stack without data (a bucket's by what it holds)

maxDamage.description: Item::getMaxDamage: its durability, 0 where it does not wear out

enchantSlots.description: Item::getEnchantSlot: Enchant::Slot bits (armor head 1, torso 2, feet 4, legs 8, sword 16, bow 32, ...; -1 every bit)

repairItems.description: The items Item::isValidRepairItem takes to repair it, where it wears out

componentBased.description: As the item registry the server sends a client has it

nbt.description: The item registry's components of a component-based item, from 1.21.60: an NBT tag as { type, name, value }

components.description: item_component's components of it, where the server sends them (1.18.11 to 1.21.50): an NBT tag as { type, name, value }

food.description: A food's, as its legacy food component has it, where the build keeps one

aliases.description: The old names the game still reads (loot tables name minecraft:fish for cod), each with the item it names

creative.description: The creative list the server sends a client, in its order

blockState.description: The block state it places, by its runtime id (its index in block_palette.nbt); null where it places none

nbt.description: The stack's own NBT, where it has some: an NBT tag as { type, name, value }

complexAliases.description: The old names whose data values became items of their own (minecraft:log), each with its items by data value
